newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel weighing domestic Bezeq offering.
newsitem.headline: Israel weighing domestic Bezeq offering.

text.p: The Government Corporations Authority will probably recommend to the government floating Bezeq Israel Telecom domestically rather than overseas, the daily newspaper Haaretz said on Monday.
Tsipi Livni, the director of the authority, told the newspaper that she would also recommend selling a controlling stake to a strategic investor at the same time.
"Of course we will not be able to sell as big a block of shares in the Tel Aviv market as we were planning to sell overseas, but we could sell shares in stages," she said.

She said the authority would present its proposals on how to sell further shares in Bezeq, Israel's main telecommunications company, within the next few weeks. The government currently controls 76 percent of Bezeq.

Livni's proposals mark a complete change in the government's stated plans to sell 25 percent of Bezeq in a global offering. The offering has been delayed mainly by problems surrounding a 10 percent stake in Bezeq Britain's Cable & Wireless acquired two years ago in the stock market.
A Cable & Wireless delegation is due to arrive in Israel this week to continue the talks on the company's future relationship with Bezeq.

Livni told Haaretz that floating Bezeq shares overseas with the Cable & Wireless issue unresolved would be more dificult than floating them in Tel Aviv. But, she said, that was not the only reason the authority was mulling a domestic offering.
Earlier this month, the cabinet voted to equalise terms between foreign and local investors acquiring shareholdings in Bezeq. A 10 percent ceiling on foreign holdings was eliminated.

In place if it, both foreign and lcoal investors must receive government approval to raise their holdings, starting at five percent and running up to 25 percent. In addition, Bezeq services were designated as "essential".
